messages:
oncall-bot: Paging @emma, @miguel, @raj — incident created: AUTH-DEP-2465. Severity: P1. Observed: spike in frontend 401s and console 5xxs.
emma: seeing repeated token_verification failures from our authz-gateway. Cause looks like upstream introspect/JWKS calls timing out toward Auth0 in us-east-1. Example error from gateway logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:03:11Z ERROR token_verify: introspect timeout id=xyz user=acct-123 code=504 upstream=auth0.us-east-1
```
miguel: confirmed. Auth0 introspect latency jumped ~8s then 504s starting 14:01 UTC. Also seeing our observability ingest (metrics/logs) delayed — dashboards aren't refreshing which is weird. Could be correlated rate limiting from vendor.
raj: product console failing to load for internal users too — hitting auth proxy which is returning 502s. Customers report inability to login via SSO. Impact: many PLG signup flows blocked.
oncall-bot: Current incident channel: #incidents. Incident lead: emma. Primary oncall: miguel. Escalation: raj.
emma: quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce introspect rate by enabling local token cache fallback (TTL short), 2) switch console auth to cached JWKS verification where possible, 3) implement temporary client-side retry/backoff guidance and 4) open vendor ticket with Auth0 + observability vendor.
lexi: can we enable verification with cached JWKS? That avoids introspect call for opaque tokens if we can verify signature. We have to detect opaque vs jwt though.
miguel: we can fast-path: for tokens that look like JWT (dot-separated), verify locally using cached jwks with TTL 5m. For opaque tokens, fall back to cached introspect results (if exist) or fail closed. Implementing now.
emma: pushing a deploy to authz-gateway to enable jwt-local-verify feature flag for traffic from console and internal APIs only. Rolling canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% if metrics look stable.
miguel: deploy started. Canary 10% at 14:09 UTC.
miguel: Canary 50% now. No new 5xxs from canary group. Introspect call volume dropped 42%.
support-bot: inbound support ticket spike. Affected customers: several orgs unable to complete sign-in; highest severity: enterprise-tenant-A, enterprise-tenant-B.
raj: I'm drafting a customer advisory note. For now mark "Investigating - 3rd party auth provider" in status page.
emma: vendor ticket opened with Auth0 (ticket #AUTH-112233). Included logs and request ids. Noted we're seeing rate-limit-like 504s and increased latency. Also opened with observability vendor (OBS-7788) re: ingestion/alerting delays.
oncall-bot: @sre-lead paged for potential cross-team coordination.
sre-lead: here. can we measure percentage of auth requests failing? miguel? we need impact quant.
miguel: overall login success rate dropped from 99.8% -> 84.2% at peak. Console access errors ~12% of internal users. Sending a short CSV with sampled request ids to the ticket.
security: any risk of token replay or tolerance changes? switching to cached jwks is safe for signed JWTs; for opaque tokens we must be careful. Avoid changing session TTLs.
emma: agreed — no session TTL extension. We are enabling cached verification only when signature verifies locally. For opaque tokens we will reduce introspect frequency and prefer previously cached introspect ttl=60s.
miguel: full rollout of feature flag complete. Introspect volume down 78% vs peak. Still seeing some 504s for specific regions. Auth0 response: "We're investigating intermittent gateway errors in us-east-1 causing elevated latencies; rate-limiting side effects possible." They requested request traces.
emma: next mitigation: add emergency route in API gateway to prefer secondary IdP (Okta) for new interactive logins where configured (we have 20% tenants with Okta). We'll programmatically route SSO flows for those tenants.
raj: implementing routing change for Okta-enabled orgs now. Will take ~10m to propagate.
raj: routing change applied for Okta tenants. Early signal: those tenants' login success improved ~90%.
product-support: queuing manual outreach to top affected customers. Recommend offering status call and ETA once vendor confirms root cause.
oncall-bot: Handoff request: emma -> miguel at 15:00 UTC for continued monitoring. Tagging incident channel for next oncall.
emma: handing off to miguel at 15:00 UTC. summary for handoff: upstream Auth0 gateway intermittent 504s; we reduced introspect pressure via cached jwks-local-verify and cached-introspect fallback; routed Okta tenants to Okta as secondary; customer impact reduced but not fully resolved for JWT-introspect heavy tenants. Vendor investigating.
miguel: taking over. I'll continue monitoring and coordinate with Auth0/OBS tickets. Next update in 15m or on severity change.
oncall-bot: Handoff acknowledged. New incident lead: miguel.
miguel: Auth0 reported mitigation: rolling restart of their us-east gateway; post-restart they report success in reducing 504s. We're seeing gradual recovery in introspect latencies.
support-bot: inbound CS notes: two enterprise customers requested immediate logs for their failed auth attempts. We provided traces and follow-up.
miguel: metrics: overall login success back to 97.6%. Console errors down to 1.5%. Still tracking a small tail of timeouts in us-east.
Auth0: vendor update in ticket AUTH-112233: root cause suspected: upstream DDoS protection misconfiguration causing traffic to hit degraded route; they applied mitigation. We requested postmortem.
emma: good. next steps: 1) prepare internal postmortem draft (SRE + Product) 2) update status page with vendor mitigation confirmation 3) roll back any temporary relaxations (we didn't change TTLs, so mostly feature flag remains for safety) 4) run regression tests for introspect fallback correctness.
product-support: scheduling a webinar readout for major customers that experienced login issues.
miguel: closing incident in 2h if no regression. leaving flags in place for 24h and will set TTL back to default after 24h of stable metrics.
oncall-bot: Incident AUTH-DEP-2465 status: Monitoring. Incident lead: miguel. Last updated 15:47 UTC.
emma: thanks everyone — great cross-team coordination. We'll capture learnings in the postmortem: (1) add better circuit-breaker around introspect calls, (2) ensure observability vendor fallback for metrics, (3) formalize elective secondary-IdP routing for critical tenants.
mitigation-summary: local jwks verify for signed JWTs; cached-introspect fallback for opaque tokens; routing to Okta for Okta-configured tenants; vendor engaged and mitigated. Customer impact: partial outage for logins and console access for some tenants; reduced significantly after mitigations.
